title: Museum Kitzbühel – Sammlung Alfons Walde
name: Museum Kitzbühel – Sammlung Alfons Walde
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum Kitzbühel in the medieval granary: the world's largest collection of masterpieces by Alfons Walde, ski history, and civic heritage.
beschreibung:
Overview

The prestigious Museum Kitzbühel is situated in the heart of the historic old town of the glamorous resort town of Kitzbühel in the Tyrolean Unterland. Housed across two historical monuments – the late-medieval former municipal granary and the adjacent southwest tower of the ancient town wall –, the museum ranks among Tyrol's most distinguished art and cultural venues. Across more than 750 square metres of exhibition space, the museum showcases the world's premier permanent collection of paintings and graphic works by the celebrated Tyrolean modernist artist Alfons Walde, alongside a rich chronicle of regional mining heritage, municipal history, and ski racing triumphs.

Alfons Walde & Collections

The Kitzbühel painter and architect Alfons Walde (1891–1958) shaped the visual image of Tyrol around the globe like virtually no other modern artist, renowned for his luminous snow-drenched alpine landscapes, whitewashed sunlit farmhouses, and dynamic ski pioneers. On the museum's top floor, more than 60 original oil paintings as well as numerous sketches, photographs, and architectural designs are showcased under optimal lighting – including iconic masterworks such as "Aufsteigender Skifahrer" (Ascending Skier) and "Tiroler Bergdörfer im Schnee" (Tyrolean Mountain Villages in the Snow). In addition to the magnificent art collection, the museum guides visitors through the region's fascinating past: from prehistoric Bronze Age relics and the golden era of copper and silver mining on the Hahnenkamm to the triumphant legacy of Kitzbühel's ski legends around Toni Sailer and the world-renowned Hahnenkamm race on the Streif. The rooftop terrace of the medieval defensive tower also affords a breathtaking panoramic view of the colourful facades of Kitzbühel's old town.

Visit & Getting There

The Museum Kitzbühel is open year-round from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (in July and August Monday to Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00; closed on Mondays during winter and the off-season). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €10.00, seniors approx. €8.50, pupils and students approx. €5.00, children up to 18 years enjoy free admission. Holders of the Kitzbüheler Gästekarte receive a discount. Getting there by train: the ÖBB station Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm is only about a five-minute walk from the museum; from Kitzbühel Hauptbahnhof (main station) it is about a 12-minute walk to the town centre. By car: via the B161 or B170 to Kitzbühel; paid parking facilities are available in the underground car park Tiefgarage Pfarrau or at the Hahnenkammbahn car park.

Tips

The entire museum building is fully accessible via a modern glass elevator and barrier-free for wheelchairs and pushchairs; a wheelchair-accessible WC is available on site. Following your art tour, take a leisurely stroll through the historic streets of Hinterstadt and Vorderstadt with their heritage-listed Gothic townhouses.
